\subsection*{Formulas --- QBF: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Formulas.QBF}.

\subsection*{Formulas --- QBF: Results}

\begin{definition}[Quantifier kind]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p007-b004}
\label{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
\leanok
Define a quantifier kind to be either existential ($\exists$) or universal ($\forall$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Quantified Boolean formula]
\lean{Complexity.QBF}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p007-b004}
\label{Complexity.QBF}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
A quantified Boolean formula consists of a finite list of quantifier kinds, whose entry
at position $i$ binds variable $i$, together with a CNF matrix over the natural-number
variables.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Recursive quantified matrix truth]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.truthAux}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p007-b004}
\label{Complexity.QBF.truthAux}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
Given a CNF matrix $m$ over natural-number variables, a list of quantifier kinds, an
assignment $\sigma:\mathbb N\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and a starting index
$i\in\mathbb N$, define truth recursively. For an empty quantifier list, the condition
is that $m$ evaluates to true under $\sigma$. For an existential quantifier followed by
a list $qs$, some Boolean value $b$ must make the recursive condition hold for $qs$ with
variable $i$ updated to $b$ and index $i+1$; for a universal quantifier, that condition
must hold for both Boolean values $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Truth of a quantified Boolean formula]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.truth}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p007-b004}
\label{Complexity.QBF.truth}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF, Complexity.QBF.truthAux}
A quantified Boolean formula is true if its CNF matrix evaluates to true under the
recursive quantification specified by its quantifier list, starting with the assignment
that sets every natural-number variable to false and with starting index $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Satisfiability from an Existential Prefix]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.satisfiable_of_exPrefix}
\label{Complexity.QBF.satisfiable_of_exPrefix}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.truthAux, Std.Sat.CNF.Satisfiable}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables, let $j$ and $i$ be natural
numbers, and let $\sigma$ be a Boolean assignment. If the prefix of $j$ existential
quantifiers starting at index $i$ is true under $\sigma$, then $m$ is satisfiable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preserving prefix agreement by updating an assignment]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.update_prefix_agreement}
\label{Complexity.QBF.update_prefix_agreement}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\sigma,\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$ and $i\in\mathbb{N}$. If $\sigma$ and $\tau$
agree at every index below $i$, then the assignment obtained from $\sigma$ by setting
its value at $i$ to $\tau(i)$ agrees with $\tau$ at every index below $i+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Truth of an Existential Prefix]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.exPrefix_of_satisfying}
\label{Complexity.QBF.exPrefix_of_satisfying}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.truthAux, Complexity.QBF.update_prefix_agreement, Complexity.eval_congr_of_lt_numVars, Std.Sat.CNF.numVars}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables, let $	au$ be a Boolean
assignment satisfying $m$, and let $j,i	ext{ be natural numbers}$ and $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ be another Boolean assignment. If $	au$ and $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ agree at every variable with index less than $i$, and the variable count of $m$
is at most $i+j$, then the prefix of $j$ existential quantifiers starting at index $i$
is true under $	ext{ let }
\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existential prefixes and satisfiability]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.truth_exPrefix_iff_satisfiable}
\label{Complexity.QBF.truth_exPrefix_iff_satisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.exPrefix_of_satisfying, Complexity.QBF.satisfiable_of_exPrefix, Complexity.QBF.truth, Std.Sat.CNF.Satisfiable, Std.Sat.CNF.numVars}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. If the
variable count of $m$ is at most $n$, then the quantified formula with $n$ successive
existential quantifiers, starting from the all-false assignment at variable index $0$,
is true if and only if $m$ is satisfiable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Truth of a Quantifier Prefix]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p007-b004}
\label{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant}
Let $P$ be a property of Boolean assignments $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to
\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. The prefix is true at an assignment when its
quantifiers can be evaluated in order starting at variable index $i$: an existential
quantifier requires some Boolean value for the current variable, while a universal
quantifier requires every Boolean value; after either choice, the assignment is updated
at index $i$ and evaluation continues at index $i+1$. An empty prefix is true exactly
when $P$ holds of the assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Truth of a quantified prefix]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.truthAux_iff_prefixTruth}
\label{Complexity.QBF.truthAux_iff_prefixTruth}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth, Complexity.QBF.Quant, Complexity.QBF.truthAux}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables, let $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ be a finite
list of existential or universal quantifiers, and let $\sigma$ be a Boolean assignment
with starting variable index $i$. The recursively quantified truth of $m$ under this
prefix is equivalent to the truth obtained by applying the same prefix to the predicate
that $m$ evaluates to true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Invariance Under Agreement on the Initial Segment]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr_agree}
\label{Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr_agree}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth, Complexity.QBF.Quant}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ and $P'$ be predicates on Boolean assignments, and let $q$ be a finite
quantifier prefix, $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ a Boolean assignment, and $i$ a natural-number starting index. Suppose that $P$
and $P'$ agree on every assignment $	au$ that agrees with $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ at all indices below $i$. Then $q$ is true under $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ at index $i$ with predicate $P$ if and only if it is true there with predicate
$P'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Invariance Under Equivalent Predicates]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr}
\label{Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth, Complexity.QBF.Quant, Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr_agree}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ and $P'$ be predicates on Boolean assignments that agree on every assignment.
For any finite quantifier prefix, Boolean assignment $	ext{ let }
\sigma$, and natural-number starting index $i$, the prefix is true with predicate $P$
exactly when it is true with predicate $P'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Truth of Concatenated Quantifier Prefixes]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_append}
\label{Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_append}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth, Complexity.QBF.Quant}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a predicate on Boolean assignments to natural-number variables, let $q$ and
$r$ be finite quantifier prefixes, and let $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ be an assignment with starting index $i$. Truth of the concatenated prefix $q$
followed by $r$ under $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ at index $i$ is equivalent to truth of $q$ under $	ext{ let }
\sigma$ at index $i$, with the predicate that the remaining prefix $r$ is true starting
at index $i+|q|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existential completion of a variable prefix]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.truthAux_exSuffix_iff}
\label{Complexity.QBF.truthAux_exSuffix_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.exPrefix_of_satisfying, Complexity.QBF.truthAux, Std.Sat.CNF.numVars}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a CNF formula over variables indexed by the natural numbers, let
$j,i\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. If the variable count of $m$
is at most $i+j$, then the formula is true under $j$ successive existential choices for
variables $i$ through $i+j-1$, starting from $\sigma$, if and only if there is an
assignment $\tau$ agreeing with $\sigma$ on every variable below $i$ such that $m$
evaluates to true under $\tau$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existential suffix after a quantified prefix]
\lean{Complexity.QBF.truth_exSuffix_of_pointwise}
\label{Complexity.QBF.truth_exSuffix_of_pointwise}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.PrefixTruth, Complexity.QBF.Quant, Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_append, Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr, Complexity.QBF.truth, Complexity.QBF.truthAux, Complexity.QBF.truthAux_exSuffix_iff, Complexity.QBF.truthAux_iff_prefixTruth, Std.Sat.CNF.numVars}
\difficulty{3}
Let $q$ be a finite list of existential or universal quantifiers, let $T$ be a CNF
formula over natural-number variables, let $G\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $P$ be a predicate
on Boolean assignments to natural-number variables. Suppose the variable count of $T$ is
at most the length of $q$ plus $G$, and for every assignment $\sigma$, there is an
assignment agreeing with $\sigma$ on all variables below the length of $q$ that
satisfies $T$ if and only if $P(\sigma)$. Then the quantified formula with prefix $q$
followed by $G$ existential quantifiers, starting from the all-false assignment at index
$0$, is true if and only if applying prefix $q$ to $P$ from that same initial assignment
is true.
\end{theorem}
